newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 17.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:

- Legal filings were made that, if proved, could result in Wall Street firms that market municipal securities paying back as much as $1 billion in illicit profits brought in at the expense of the Treasury and municipal borrowers.
- The Boeing Co is on the brink of becoming an even bigger player than it has been on the American foreign policy stage.
- Fox, in its feud with Time Warner, has taken out newspaper advertisements warning football fans in certain markets that they might not be able to see this year's Super Bowl on TV.
- The proposed merger of Boeing and McDonnell Douglas received the blessings of Wall Street and aerospace analysts and the Pentagon expressed only minor reservations.

- In light of the Boeing/McDonnell Douglas merger, Airbus faces a tougher struggle in its goal of seizing half the commercial jet market, though the huge Chinese market may smile on the company because it tends to buy aircraft from more than one supplier to keep competition keen.
- Safeway said that Vons, a Southern California food chain, accepted a revised bid, worth $1.56 billion.
- Industrial production surged by nine-tenths of one percent in November.
- A late slide in computer shares, led by IBM, pushed the stock market down in volatile trading.
- Bristol Hotel said it would acquire 61 Holiday Inns from Bass of Britain for $659 million.
- Conseco said it planned to buy Pioneer Financial Services for $417 million.
- The former head of government bond trading at Daiwa Bank in New York was sentenced to four years in prison for concealing $1.1 billion in trading losses.
- Shares in Value Line have turned weak after rising in the weeks following word that a fight for control within the founding family had been resolved.
- China's two stock markets fell about 10 percent.
